answer: DeepWalk does not require a graph of agents interacting with pages. It works on any undirected (or directed) graph of nodes and edges. It generates truncated random walks from each node, treats each walk as a sentence, and trains a skip-gram model on the sequences. The method is agnostic to node semantics. It would only involve agents and pages if the input graph were a user-page interaction graph, such as a bipartite network, and even then the walks would simply traverse whatever edges exist, with no special condition. The premise of the question is therefore not an actual requirement of DeepWalk.
